sections.heading: Findings
sections.body: This morning, I interviewed a candidate with a PhD in Engineering. Smart background, solid resume… but when I asked a basic question about unit testing, I swear I heard keys tapping. Then—after an oddly long pause—I got an answer. Not his answer, but something suspiciously polished, like it had just come out of an AI thesaurus. Vocabulary shift. Tone shift. Everything. It was like talking to a different person. [E1] Having a competent, skilled interviewer engaging early on in your process — someone who can go off-script, who knows how to dig, who can read when something feels "off" — is more important than ever. The interview process isn’t just a technical filter. It’s a BS detector, a vibe check, and yes, sometimes a Turing test. [E2] The interviewer asked a candidate with a PhD in Engineering a basic question about unit testing [E3]. Vocabulary shift. Tone shift. Everything. It was like talking to a different person. [E4] The interviewer asked the candidate 'What questions do you have for me?' and observed the candidate pause before giving a response that sounded like ChatGPT had wrapped a TED Talk [E5]. Having a competent, skilled interviewer engaging early on in your process — someone who can go off-script, who knows how to dig, who can read when something feels "off" — is more important than ever. [E6] The best implementations use a video avatar and genuine two-way conversation — not a chatbot filling out a scorecard. [E8] An AI interviewer applies the same rubric to every candidate consistently, while a human interviewer's rubric application shifts with mood, fatigue, time of day, and how many candidates they have already seen [E10].

This morning, I interviewed a candidate with a PhD in Engineering. Smart background, solid resume… but when I asked a basic question about unit testing, I swear I heard keys tapping.
Vocabulary shift. Tone shift. Everything. It was like talking to a different person.

When I asked, "What questions do you have for me?"—a softball for any prepared candidate—he paused again. Then rattled off a response that sounded like ChatGPT had just wrapped a TED Talk on “Questions That Impress Interviewers.”
Having a competent, skilled interviewer engaging early on in your process — someone who can go off-script, who knows how to dig, who can read when something feels "off"—is more important than ever.
The best implementations use a video avatar and genuine two-way conversation — not a chatbot filling out a scorecard.

An AI interviewer applies the same rubric to candidate 1 and candidate 1,000. A human interviewer applies a version of the rubric that shifts with mood, fatigue, time of day, and how many candidates they have already seen that week.

An AI interviewer is software that conducts a structured interview with a candidate, asks follow-up questions based on the candidate's responses, evaluates the answers against a predefined rubric, and produces a scored report.

An AI interviewer for technical screening is an automated system that runs a structured technical interview coding, system design, or role-specific questions without a human interviewer present. It uses a large language model plus a rubric to ask questions, follow up on candidate answers, evaluate responses, and produce a scored report.
